messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The DIC of current model is the same as that of saturated model.
parts:
Response data(y) is a binary data, (that is 1 or 0)
Thus, the likelihood was selected as "binomial" with N.trials = 1
The code is like below:


#### start code ####
mesh1<-inla.mesh.2d( boundary =boundry)
pc_spde = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh1, prior.range = c(1, 0.01), prior.sigma = c(1, .01), constr=TRUE)
pc.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field", n.spde=pc_spde$n.spde)

model_data<-model.matrix(as.formula(~0+a+b+c), data = my_data)
X<-as.data.frame(model_data)
str(X)

stack.est <- inla.stack(data = list(y=y),
                        A = list(A.est,1),
                        effects = list(pc.index,
                                       data.frame(X, Intercept= 1)),
                        tag="est")

formula_sp<- as.formula(y~0+Intercept+a+b+c + f(spatial.field, model=pc_spde))

spatial <- inla(formula_sp, family = "binomial",Ntrials=1,
                data = inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde=pc_spde), 
                control.family = list(link = "logit"),
                control.compute= list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE),
                control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est),compute=TRUE))
#### end code ####


Thank you.
